reason: The proof uses the standard characterization of continuity that the inverse image of every closed set is closed; the irrelevant group-theory rule candidates are not applicable.
text:
Since \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb R\), the inverse image \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). But
\[
f^{-1}(\{0\})=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=Z(f).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed in \(X\).
